draft.title: Inventory management
card: Holding inventory ties up cash, and stock can go missing or go out of date. Good management reduces these problems.
Regular counts compare stock on the shelves with the records, so losses are found early. Setting expected levels shows when to reorder and warns of too much or too little stock.
Rotating stock means selling older items first, so goods do not spoil or go out of date. Stocking goods that sell together, such as phone cases with phones, can lift sales.
Strong controls, such as locked storerooms and limits on who can access or change stock records, help stop theft and mistakes.
draft.remember: Good inventory management keeps stock available, fresh and safe without tying up too much cash.

a.q: Ravi's deli in Shepparton sells fresh dairy goods. Which practice best stops older items from passing their use-by date?
opts: Selling the older items first
Buying much more stock each week
Counting stock once a year
Selling the newest items first
a.why: Rotating stock by selling older items first means goods are used before they expire. Buying more stock would tie up more cash and leave more to spoil.
a.clue: Think about which items should leave the shelf first.

b.q: Ella's hardware store in Wodonga holds far more paint than it sells. What is the main problem this causes?
opts: Cash is tied up in unsold stock
Gross profit is overstated
Sales revenue is too high
Stock cannot be counted
b.why: Stock that sits unsold uses up cash that could be used elsewhere. It does not raise sales revenue or gross profit, which come only from goods sold.
b.clue: Money spent on paint is not available for other uses.

b.best: Cash is tied up in unsold stock

problems.detail: The clue 'Money spent on paint is not available for other uses' restates the right option, so students can pick it without knowing the idea.

The why explains where sales revenue and gross profit come from ('which come only from goods sold'). Gross profit belongs to point 3 (Cost of sales and gross profit), so it should only be mentioned here, not explained.

b.q: Ella's hardware store in Wodonga holds far more paint than it sells. What is the main problem this causes?
opts: Cash is tied up in unsold stock
The store is likely to run out of paint
The store will soon need to reorder paint
Anyone can change the stock records
b.why: Paint that sits unsold holds money the store could have used for wages, bills or other goods. Running out and needing to reorder are problems of too little stock, not too much.
b.clue: Think about what Ella spent to fill her shelves.
